signals.signal: [global] Euronet renamed its EFT Processing Segment to 'Payments Infrastructure' (PI) in May 2026 and Money Transfer to 'Cross-Border Payments', formalised in the Q2 2026 10-Q filed 04/08/2026. PI now spans 57,071 installed ATMs and approximately 641,000 POS terminals across 70 countries. The 10-Q states PI revenue growth was 'driven by continued growth in acquiring, REN infrastructure sales and contributions from the CoreCard acquisition' — i.e. the growth engine is software/processing/acquiring, not ATMs. The filing also newly enumerates 'banknote recycling' as a named PI revenue source alongside cardless payment, tax refund, licence fees, professional services and maintenance fees.
signals.source_name: Euronet Worldwide Form 10-Q for Q2 2026 (SEC EDGAR, CIK 1029199)
signals.implies: Euronet is repositioning from an ATM deployer to a full payments-infrastructure vendor, which means it will now bid against Printec on more than ATM outsourcing: card issuing/processing (Ren, CoreCard), acquiring and terminal management. The explicit appearance of banknote recycling as a revenue line is the most Printec-adjacent detail — it is the same cash-automation revenue Printec sells through Glory/Sesami TCRs and NCR recyclers. Printec should stop pitching Euronet as 'the ATM fee company' to footprint banks and instead defend on multivendor depth (NCR x-core), telemetry/monitoring, OptiCash cash optimisation and open TMS, where a single-vendor infrastructure platform locks the bank in.
signals.likelihood: In force now; platform bundling pitches to footprint banks ongoing
signals.followup: Pull the FY2026 10-K segment note when filed to see whether banknote-recycling revenue is broken out; ask footprint bank accounts whether Euronet has pitched a bundled acquiring+ATM+recycling proposal.

signals.signal: [global] Euronet's ATM estate has effectively stopped growing while its revenue accelerates elsewhere. Q2 2026 10-Q operating data: active ATMs 57,071 at 30/06/2026 vs 56,760 a year earlier (+1%); average installed ATMs for the six months 53,050 vs 53,138 (a 0%/slight decline). PI revenue rose 11% to USD 377.1m but PI operating income rose only 2% to USD 86.1m, with direct operating costs up 18% — real margin compression on the ATM/outsourcing base. Transactions processed rose 15% to 4,279m, so volume is being won at lower unit economics.
signals.source_name: Euronet Worldwide Form 10-Q for Q2 2026 (SEC EDGAR, CIK 1029199)
signals.implies: A flat estate plus compressing ATM margins means Euronet's incentive to buy bank fleets on generous terms is weakening, and the cost pressure will push it to raise surcharges rather than expand. That is Printec's opening: footprint banks weighing 'outsource to Euronet vs keep the fleet' can now be shown that the outsourcer's own economics are deteriorating. Printec should lead with owned-fleet TCO — NCR dispense/deposit/recycling hardware plus x-core multivendor software, device telemetry/monitoring and managed field services — as the alternative that keeps brand, fee and customer control with the bank.
signals.likelihood: Trend visible now; likely to persist through FY2026
signals.followup: Re-key the Q3 2026 10-Q (due ~early Nov 2026) for active-ATM count and PI operating margin; build a one-page TCO counter-argument for Greek, Croatian and Romanian bank accounts.

signals.entity: Euronet Worldwide — ATM network cash risk
signals.signal: [global] The Q2 2026 10-Q discloses that under its contracts with financial institutions in the Payments Infrastructure segment Euronet is responsible for damage to ATMs and theft of ATM network cash, and that the balance of cash in its ATM networks for which it was responsible at 30/06/2026 was approximately USD 935.0 million. This is the first-order commercial reason banks find ATMaaS attractive: the outsourcer absorbs the cash, insurance and CIT (cash-in-transit) risk, not just the hardware.
signals.source_name: Euronet Worldwide Form 10-Q for Q2 2026 (SEC EDGAR, CIK 1029199)
signals.implies: When a footprint bank says it wants to outsource ATMs, the real driver is usually balance-sheet and cash-risk transfer rather than technology. Printec loses those conversations if it only offers hardware and field service. The defensible counter is a managed-service wrap: NCR ATMs plus x-core, device telemetry/monitoring, physical ATM security and NCR APTRA OptiCash cash optimisation, which cuts the bank's cash holding and replenishment cost without handing the estate — and the customer relationship — to Euronet. Printec should partner explicitly with a local CIT firm on each bid to close the risk-transfer gap.
signals.likelihood: Standing structural driver of every footprint ATMaaS bid
signals.followup: Package an OptiCash + telemetry + CIT-partner 'risk-managed owned fleet' proposition for Erste Croatia, BCR and Raiffeisen Serbia before Euronet pitches ATMaaS there.

signals.entity: Euronet Worldwide — Q2 2026 earnings call commentary
signals.signal: [global] On the Q2 2026 earnings call (30/07/2026) management named NO new ATM-as-a-Service or ATM-outsourcing win. Every named win was outside the Printec footprint: Unibanca in Peru (multi-year Ren + CoreCard credit-issuing deal, explicitly 'displacing an incumbent processor'), Upgrade in the US (CoreCard), and a Costa Rican bank sponsorship to grow the IAD network. Europe featured only as a headwind: US-to-Europe airline bookings running 5-8% below the peak 2025 booking window and European travellers 'more selective with discretionary spending', with management noting 'a little bit of improvement as we go into the third quarter'. On Greece, management said only that it had expanded on the previously announced CrediaBank merchant-services acquisition and launched a merchant-acquiring referral programme that added 4,200 new merchants in the quarter. Adjusted EPS was USD 2.82, up 10%, the fifth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth; digital accelerators were 26% of YTD revenue growing 31% in the quarter.
signals.source_name: Euronet (EEFT) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript, The Motley Fool
signals.implies: For a full quarter Euronet added no new European bank ATM-outsourcing mandate that it was willing to name — its displacement engine right now is card issuing/processing in Latin America, not CEE/SEE ATM estates. That is a window: Printec's ATM and self-service pursuits in Greece, Croatia, Romania, Serbia and Bulgaria face no fresh Euronet reference win to bid against. The 4,200-merchant referral programme is the real footprint threat and it is a POS/acquiring one — it presses directly on Printec's Verifone/Castles terminal and TMS line in Greece.
signals.likelihood: Next disclosure point is Q3 2026 results (~late Oct 2026)
signals.followup: Re-key the Q3 2026 call for any named European ATMaaS win; map the Greek merchant-acquiring referral programme's channel partners, since they are the route Euronet is using to reach merchants Printec's terminal business serves.

signals.entity: Euronet Card Services Greece — ATM surcharge regime
signals.signal: [STANDING — dated 2025] Greek law 5222/2025 caps the charge a third-party ATM operator may levy on a cardholder at EUR 1.50, but exempts arrangements where the payment service provider holds a direct or indirect stake in the ATM operator. Greek coverage of the CrediaBank/Euronet announcement (08/01/2026) sets out that CrediaBank and Euronet have no equity or administrative relationship and that the zero-fee access CrediaBank customers get across Euronet's 2,500+ Greek ATMs rests purely on a commercial bilateral agreement. Euronet separately operates more than 2,200 off-branch ATMs in Greece after 25+ years in the market and has been rolling out a 'free-of-charge' ATM network via supermarket-chain agreements since 2024.
signals.source_name: FinancialReport.gr — CrediaBank/Euronet zero-fee arrangement and law 5222/2025
signals.implies: The EUR 1.50 cap squeezes the surcharge economics that fund Euronet's Greek independent-ATM estate and pushes it to monetise instead through bank bilateral agreements and full-fleet management contracts — exactly the CrediaBank structure. For Printec this means the Greek battleground shifts from off-branch IAD placement to who runs the banks' OWN fleets. Printec should press Greek banks on the point that a capped-fee environment makes an owned, Printec-maintained estate with NCR recyclers plus x-core and telemetry cheaper to run than paying an outsourcer whose fee income the state has just capped.
signals.likelihood: Standing regime; shapes every Greek ATM commercial in the next 18 months
signals.followup: Obtain the text of law 5222/2025 from the Greek Government Gazette and confirm the exact scope of the stake-based exemption; check whether any Greek bank has taken an equity stake in an ATM operator in response.

signals.entity: Euronet Services spol. s r.o. (Czech Republic)
signals.signal: [global] Euronet is now under EU-level regulatory attack in a Printec footprint country. Czech Pirate MEP Marketa Gregorova submitted a written question to the European Commission on 09/06/2026 alleging manipulative interface design (dark patterns) and dynamic currency conversion (DCC) practices at Euronet ATMs, asking whether they are compatible with the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive and the cross-border payments regulation. On 24/06/2026 she escalated to calling for legislative change that would bind all operators, not only Euronet, citing a documented case where a EUR 1,000 withdrawal carried roughly CZK 4,250 of cost, which Euronet itemised as a 13.95% mark-up over the ECB reference rate plus a fixed EUR 3.95 fee. Euronet published a formal rebuttal on its Czech newsroom on 19/06/2026 (Czech director Ondrej Kozak: full compliance with EU and national law) and followed with defensive explainers on 26/06 and 29/06/2026. Context: Euronet introduced a DAF (Direct Access Fee — a flat charge levied by the ATM operator on the withdrawal itself, separate from the cardholder's own bank fee) on DOMESTIC Czech cards from October 2025, and its own newsroom has previously put its Czech estate at roughly 10% of the national ATM total with about 300 in Prague.
signals.source_name: Respekt (MEP question, 09/06/2026); Tyden.cz (legislative push, 24/06/2026); Euronet Czech newsroom rebuttal (19/06/2026)
signals.implies: Sustained political and EU-institutional pressure on the surcharge/DCC model is the most plausible route by which Czech banks reclaim brand and fee control over cash access — which means owned or bank-branded fleets rather than reliance on an independent deployer. That is directly Printec's lane: NCR ATMs, x-core multivendor software, telemetry/monitoring and managed field services. Printec should brief Czech and Slovak bank accounts that regulatory risk now attaches to the outsourced-IAD cash-access model, and position a bank-branded shared-ATM alternative before any Commission response lands.
signals.likelihood: Commission response and any legislative follow-through likely 6-18 months; Czech bank reaction sooner
signals.followup: Track the European Commission's written answer to Gregorova's question and any CNB (Czech National Bank) or Ministry of Finance statement; watch for a Czech bank tendering an owned or shared branded ATM fleet.

signals.entity: Euronet ATMs (group newsroom) — ATMaaS sales narrative
signals.signal: [global] On 03/08/2026 Euronet published 'Every ATM Tells a Story. Here's What It Takes to Keep It Running' on its group ATM newsroom, a structured cost-of-ownership argument built on the Datos Insights study 'The Future of ATM Economics: Ensuring Sustainable Cash Access in an Evolving Market'. It breaks offsite ATM operating cost into connectivity and payment-scheme integration, continuous regulatory/security compliance and software upgrades, site selection and lifecycle management, and cash availability — the standard build-up used to argue a bank should not own ATMs. It follows the November 2025 piece 'ATM as a Service: How ATM Outsourcing is Transforming Banking?' and the December 2025 'The Future of ATM Economics'. This is a deliberate, repeated pre-sell of the ATMaaS TCO case to European banks.
signals.implies: This is the exact argument Printec will meet in every footprint ATM refresh and self-service tender over the next 12 months, and it is aimed at CFOs, not IT. Printec needs a written counter-model that concedes the cost categories but shows they are addressable without surrendering the estate: x-core multivendor software removes OEM lock-in, telemetry/monitoring cuts field visits and downtime, APTRA OptiCash cuts cash holding and CIT frequency, and Printec managed/field services absorb the lifecycle work. Whoever brings the numbers first sets the frame in accounts such as Erste Croatia, BCR, Raiffeisen Serbia and OTP/Raiffeisen Albania.
signals.likelihood: Active sales campaign now; will appear in footprint bids over 6-12 months
signals.followup: Obtain the Datos Insights 'Future of ATM Economics' study (Euronet-sponsored) and build a line-by-line Printec rebuttal deck for footprint bank CFOs.

signals.entity: Euronet Magyarorszag — Community ATM programme vs Act XVIII of 2025
signals.signal: [global] Hungary's Act XVIII of 2025 and the accompanying MNB decree require an ATM in every settlement above 1,000 inhabitants by end-2025 and in every settlement above 500 inhabitants by END-2026, with the MNB allocating named settlements to named banks (1,039 settlements were identified as having no ATM). The law expressly permits banks to install and operate ATMs jointly. Euronet, historically concentrated in Hungarian city centres and tourist locations, markets a 'Kozossegi ATM' (Community ATM) programme to municipalities and organisations under which the municipality supplies a site free of charge and Euronet takes full responsibility for installing and operating the machine, expanding an estate its own material puts at roughly 600 ATMs in Hungary. Euronet's dated Hungarian newsroom is stale (latest post 20/06/2025) and the Community ATM material carries no verifiable publication date, so the estate figure and programme scale are UNCONFIRMED and must not be quoted as current.
signals.source_name: Index.hu (Magyar Kozlony decree on mandatory small-settlement ATM installation) + Store Insider (Euronet Kozossegi ATM programme, undated)
signals.implies: The end-2026 deadline forces Hungarian banks to place ATMs in low-volume rural sites where a bank-owned machine will never pay for itself, and the joint-operation clause plus Euronet's municipality programme make Euronet the obvious shared-deployer answer. Because allocation is by MNB decree rather than public tender, there is no procurement portal to watch — this has to be worked bank by bank. Printec's opening is the alternative to handing those sites to Euronet: low-cost NCR dispense ATMs plus x-core, remote telemetry/monitoring to keep field visits down, and a managed-service contract sized for low-transaction rural sites, sold jointly to two or more banks sharing one machine.
signals.likelihood: Hard regulatory deadline end-2026; bank decisions being taken now
signals.followup: Find a dated 2026 Hungarian source for Euronet's Community ATM wins and current HU estate (portfolio.hu, penzcentrum.hu, bank360.hu); obtain the MNB settlement-to-bank allocation list and approach the allocated banks with a shared-ATM managed-service proposition before end-2026.
